name: Jekamiah
overview: Jekamiah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Jehoiachin, also called Jeconiah. His identity is rooted in his lineage within the royal family of Judah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:18. There are no additional notes or details about his life beyond this familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Jekamiah means 'YHWH will establish,' reflecting a theologically significant Hebrew meaning. This proper name was not given directly by God but carries a meaning that emphasizes God's sustaining power, as noted in 1 Chronicles 3:18.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jekamiah as the son of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah), situating him within the Davidic line of Judah. No other familial relationships are detailed beyond this connection in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jekamiah's significance lies in his place within the genealogy of Judah's royal house, linking him to Jehoiachin, a key figure in the history of Israel's monarchy. His mention in 1 Chronicles 3:18 serves to affirm the continuity of the Davidic lineage, which is foundational to understanding the messianic promises fulfilled in Christ. Although little is recorded about his personal deeds, his inclusion underscores God's faithfulness in preserving the royal line through generations.
